chapter: Reel 2: Los Angeles musicians, the Apex and Cotton Club
title: Lionel Hampton's touring troupe and Howard introducing him to Gladys
summary: Howard was head of Lionel's travelling act of six to eight performers; Mrs. Howard says Paul introduced Lionel to his future wife Gladys.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: No, no. He probably stayed here all the time. Anybody else in that period you know? I think we
Yeah.
You can tell him about Lionel's band and the troupe that he travelled through the North with?
No, I didn't.
You know about that?
Yeah, I know. I was in the band.
Let's have it.
I was in the band.
You must have been something. You remember about that, then.
Yeah, I was in the band.
Why don't you tell us something about that band.
And he was-- weren't you temporary manager? He introduced Lionel and his wife, Gladys.
You did?
Yeah, to Gladys.
He introduced them.
Yeah.
Before they were married.
What do you mean? She was actually an entertainer, too?
No --
No, no, she wasn't.

She was a modiste, but seemingly, a bunch of the boys used to go up to her house at times, and at the time, Lionel was with Paul. I don't know how they got up there, but I know that Paul introduced Gladys to Lionel.
So right away they started going together? How'd that come about?
I don't know how it come about.
But did she start travelling with Lionel then?
No.
No, no.
No, because he wasn't travelling then.
I see. What about this trip with Lionel, that you were managing the group? Can you tell us something about that?
I was just the head of the group, that's all.
Were you arranging some of the music or anything like that?
No, no.
Just sort of keeping everything in order.
Keeping things in order and keeping them all in order.
What kind of leader was he at that
time? Was he cool or --
Who?
Lionel.
Lionel? Oh, he was cool. He was --- yeah, he was cool, all right.
I mean, he was handling the business and everything, or you did that?
No, I did that.
But he was still doing what he does, jumping up on the drums and things like that.
Yep.
Was it a big group or small?
No, it was a big group.
I think there were about six or eight, six or eight members in that group. These were performers. We had an act. Oh, it was more than -- I can't remember just now just how many there were.
Let's see, somebody else --
But he wasn't playing vibes then.
He was just --
Just playing drums.
Yeah, right. What about the piano? Did he play piano at all, like he does sometimes?
Who?
Lionel, at that time.
Yeah, yeah, he played piano.
He did play piano?
Yeah. Could always play the blues.
Yeah. So the vibes came later.
No, he played the vibes, too. But they weren't so prominent as they are now.
